q: Producers are green plants which photosynthesise to produce food.
e: True. Producers are green plants which photosynthesise to produce food. Producers, mainly green plants, convert light to chemical energy.

q: The consumers that subsist on herbivores are secondary consumers.
e: False. It is not true that the consumers that subsist on herbivores are secondary consumers. Consumers get energy by eating other organisms.

q: Decomposers are organisms that break down dead material and help to recycle nutrients, and are also termed as reducers.
e: True. Decomposers are organisms that break down dead material and help to recycle nutrients, and are also termed as reducers. Decomposers such as bacteria and fungi break down dead material and recycle nutrients. An extra chromosome 21 produces Down's syndrome.

q: The physical environment consists of all living components of the ecosystem.
e: False. It is not true that the physical environment consists of all living components of the ecosystem. The environment is everything around an organism, biotic and abiotic. An ecosystem is a community plus its physical environment, linked by energy and materials.

q: Abiotic factors are non-living physical or chemical factors.
e: True. Abiotic factors are non-living physical or chemical factors. Abiotic factors are the non-living parts of the environment.

q: Soil conditions, such as clay content, nitrate level, particle size, water content and pH, are examples of biotic factors.
e: False. It is not true that soil conditions, such as clay content, nitrate level, particle size, water content and pH, are examples of biotic factors. Biotic factors are the living parts of the environment.

q: Biotic factors include availability of food and competition for food resources, predation, symbiosis, disease and presence of pollinating insects.
e: True. Biotic factors include availability of food and competition for food resources, predation, symbiosis, disease and presence of pollinating insects. Predation is one biotic interaction that structures communities. Many insects breathe through a tracheal system, not lungs.

q: A habitat is the place where an organism lives.
e: True. A habitat is the place where an organism lives.

q: All the organisms of a particular species found in an ecosystem at a certain time form the community.
e: False. It is not true that all the organisms of a particular species found in an ecosystem at a certain time form the community. An ecosystem is a community plus its physical environment, linked by energy and materials. A community is all the populations living together in an area.

q: The populations of all species found in an ecosystem at a particular time form the community.
e: True. The populations of all species found in an ecosystem at a particular time form the community. An ecosystem is a community plus its physical environment, linked by energy and materials. A community is all the populations living together in an area.

q: In any food chain, the arrow ($\rightarrow$) means 'is eaten by', and its direction indicates the flow of energy in the chain.
e: True. In any food chain, the arrow (rightarrow) means 'is eaten by', and its direction indicates the flow of energy in the chain. Food chains show how chemical energy flows from producers to consumers. A food chain is one linear feeding path from producer onward.

q: The different stages in a food chain (producer, primary consumer and secondary consumer) are called ecological pyramids.
e: False. It is not true that the different stages in a food chain (producer, primary consumer and secondary consumer) are called ecological pyramids. A food chain is one linear feeding path from producer onward.

q: Food webs give us more information than food chains, but they do not show the role of the decomposers.
e: True. Food webs give us more information than food chains, but they do not show the role of the decomposers. Decomposers such as bacteria and fungi break down dead material and recycle nutrients.

q: Pyramids of numbers represent the numbers of organisms in each trophic level in a food chain, irrespective of their mass.
e: True. Pyramids of numbers represent the numbers of organisms in each trophic level in a food chain, irrespective of their mass. A food chain is one linear feeding path from producer onward. Trophic levels are feeding steps in a food chain.

q: Pyramids of biomass show the total mass of the organisms in each trophic level, irrespective of their numbers.
e: True. Pyramids of biomass show the total mass of the organisms in each trophic level, irrespective of their numbers. Trophic levels are feeding steps in a food chain.

q: In the 'oak tree' food chain, the total biomass increases at each trophic level.
e: False. It is not true that in the 'oak tree' food chain, the total biomass increases at each trophic level. A food chain is one linear feeding path from producer onward. Trophic levels are feeding steps in a food chain.

q: If birds in a food chain are parasitised by nematode worms, the pyramid of numbers takes on a very strange appearance because of the large numbers of parasites on each bird.
e: True. If birds in a food chain are parasitised by nematode worms, the pyramid of numbers takes on a very strange appearance because of the large numbers of parasites on each bird. A food chain is one linear feeding path from producer onward. Birds are warm-blooded vertebrates with feathers, not fur.

q: The pyramid of biomass for a parasitised food chain has a true pyramid shape because the total biomass of the nematode worms must be less than that of the bird they parasitise.
e: True. A food chain is one linear feeding path from producer onward. Birds are warm-blooded vertebrates with feathers, not fur.

q: When a rabbit eats grass, all of the materials in the grass plant end up as rabbit tissue.
e: False. It is not true that when a rabbit eats grass, all of the materials in the grass plant end up as rabbit tissue.

q: Photosynthesis 'fixes' sunlight energy into chemical energy such as glucose and starch.
e: True. Photosynthesis 'fixes' sunlight energy into chemical energy such as glucose and starch. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light. Glucose is the hexose sugar made in photosynthesis and burned in respiration.

q: If the energy released in respiration is used for other processes then it will, eventually escape as heat from the organism.
e: True. If the energy released in respiration is used for other processes then it will, eventually escape as heat from the organism. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing.

q: Only about 10% of the energy entering a trophic level is passed on to the next trophic level.
e: True. Only about 10% of the energy entering a trophic level is passed on to the next trophic level. Trophic levels are feeding steps in a food chain.

q: Food chains may not have more than five trophic levels because there is not enough energy left for another trophic level.
e: True. Food chains may not have more than five trophic levels because there is not enough energy left for another trophic level. Food chains show how chemical energy flows from producers to consumers. Trophic levels are feeding steps in a food chain.

q: In certain parts of the world, some marine food chains have six trophic levels because of the huge amount of light energy reaching the surface water.
e: True. In certain parts of the world, some marine food chains have six trophic levels because of the huge amount of light energy reaching the surface water. Food chains show how chemical energy flows from producers to consumers. Trophic levels are feeding steps in a food chain.
